title: FieldLock: integration probe for constrained decoder behavior and token-boundary field locking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Investigate and validate a 'field-lock' approach for constrained decoding in JSON mode: ensure the decoder can lock individual JSON fields across streaming partial emits, enforce token-boundary integrity for field values, and provide deterministic fallbacks when locks conflict or are truncated. This ticket covers integration tests, fuzz scenarios, telemetry hooks, and a small repair shim prototype that can reconstruct partial fields from subsequent stream chunks.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end test harness that simulates interleaved tool calls and partial JSON emissions reproduces previously observed field-splitting failures at least 10x more reliably

Decoder implements per-field lock metadata such that when a field start token is emitted and not closed within N tokens, the system can trigger a repair path that attempts safe reassembly without violating the schema
Telemetry exposes metrics: field_lock_acquired, field_lock_released, field_lock_conflict, field_repair_attempt, field_repair_success, and per-model failure rates
A documented fallback policy used by the runtime (append-truncate, sentinel-insert, or abort-and-fallback-to-plain-mode) with measurable rollout plan and canary gating
Automated CI jobs covering deterministic seeds for fuzzed partial-streams, and integration tests run in the runtime-1.18 canary lane
test_plan: Build a targeted harness that replays recorded partial-stream traces and synthetic adversarial sequences. For each sequence run the following permutations: (1) streaming enabled vs disabled, (2) decoder with field-locks on/off, (3) fallback policy set to append-truncate / sentinel / abort. Validate output against schema assertions and compute repair success rates. Capture timing impact on tail latency for sequences that trigger locks.
test_cases: TC-01: Simple field-split - value split across two stream chunks, expect successful reassembly
TC-02: Nested object field-split with interleaved toolcall tokens, expect repair shim reconstructs nested value without schema violation
TC-03: Long value truncated by token limit then resumed by subsequent chunk, policy append-truncate vs sentinel behaviors compared
TC-04: Conflicting writes - two concurrent streams attempt to emit same field name, expect conflict metric and deterministic fallback to model-variant
TC-05: Fuzz injection - random token drops in middle of quoted string to validate decoder robustness and repair success distribution
TC-06: Backpressure scenario - batching delays cause partial emits to exceed lock timeout, confirm lock expiry and graceful recovery
telemetry: Instrument hooks inside the constrained-decoder to emit labeled spans for lock lifecycle events, attach token-count histograms and per-request model variant tags. Expose a dashboard tile for failure rate by model and route and add an alert when field_repair_success < 95% for any active canary.
notes: Trade-offs considered: fine-grained per-field locks raise overhead but reduce global rollback frequency; evaluated token-budget vs latency impact
Prototype shim will be implemented in the runtime as an optional binary flag guarded by canary config
Security: repair shim must avoid retaining plaintext of customer data beyond repair window; follow existing KMS/audit patterns
We should coordinate with Console team to surface lock metrics on per-route dashboards before broad rollout
